findings.issue_text: No double-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock in GetWebAssets, so every goroutine that saw a nil cache under the RLock redundantly rebuilds the assets (manifest read, JSON decode) instead of returning early when the cache is already populated

In setting.Dev mode the fast path is always bypassed and the exclusive Lock() is held across the filesystem read and JSON parse of the manifest, fully serializing concurrent index-page requests behind disk I/O; the lock should be skipped when not caching or the result built outside the lock
No test exercises concurrent GetWebAssets calls under -race, so neither the original data race nor the redundant-rebuild behavior is covered

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In setting.Dev mode the fast path is always bypassed and the exclusive Lock() is held across the filesystem read and JSON parse of the manifest, fully serializing concurrent index-page requests behind disk I/O; the lock should be skipped when not caching or the result built outside the lock

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global RWMutex and changes GetWebAssets to always take an exclusive Lock() (with defer Unlock()) whenever it doesn’t hit the cached fast-path. Since the fast-path is explicitly disabled in setting.Dev (the `cfg.Env != setting.Dev` condition), every call in Dev will take the exclusive lock and hold it for the entire remainder of the function. This is verifiable from the diff and will serialize concurrent callers in Dev regardless of whether caching is desired. Given GetWebAssets’ purpose (loading web assets), it’s reasonable and grounded to say the lock will cover the manifest-loading work that follows, creating a performance/concurrency regression in Dev mode.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only changes the implementation of GetWebAssets by adding an RWMutex and a cache read/lock pattern. It does not add/remove/modify any tests, and from this diff alone you cannot verify whether tests exist elsewhere that exercise concurrent GetWebAssets calls under `-race` (or cover rebuild behavior). Therefore the proposed finding is about test coverage that is not verifiable from the diff itself (even though the new code could still allow redundant rebuilds due to no re-check after acquiring the write lock).
